title: Heading
summary: Titles a page or section and builds the document outline.
description: Separate the semantic level (h1–h6) from the visual size so outline and style can vary independently. Never skip levels for looks: screen reader users jump between headings to navigate.

title: Text
summary: Renders body copy with type-scale tokens for size, weight and colour.
description: The base primitive for any run of text. Exposes variants (body, caption, overline) instead of raw font sizes, and an `as` prop so a paragraph, span or label can share the same styling.

title: Link
summary: Navigates to another page, URL or anchor.
description: If it goes somewhere, it's a Link (<a href>); if it does something, it's a Button. Links must be distinguishable by more than colour (underline) and should flag external targets.

title: Label
summary: Names a form control so users and assistive tech know what it is.
description: Bound to its control via htmlFor/id, which also makes the text clickable to focus the input. Placeholders are not a label substitute: they vanish on typing and often fail contrast.

title: Code / Kbd
summary: Shows inline code snippets or keyboard keys in a monospace style.
description: <code> marks machine text like `npm install`; <kbd> marks keys the user presses, like ⌘ K. For multi-line snippets use a CodeBlock with syntax highlighting and a copy button.

title: Blockquote
summary: Sets apart a quotation from another source.
description: Use the semantic <blockquote> with an optional cite. Don't use it just to indent or highlight text — that's a Callout's job.

title: List
summary: Groups related items as bulleted, numbered or unstyled rows.
description: Ordered (<ol>) when sequence matters, unordered (<ul>) when it doesn't. Screen readers announce the item count, so keep list semantics even when removing bullets visually.

title: Prose
summary: Styles long-form rich content (markdown, CMS HTML) with sensible rhythm.
description: A wrapper that applies vertical rhythm, measure (~65ch) and element styles to content you don't control, like rendered markdown. Keeps app components free of document typography.

title: Box
summary: A generic container that applies spacing, colour and border tokens.
description: The lowest-level layout primitive: a div that only accepts design tokens (padding, background, radius). Other layout components are often built on top of it.

title: Stack
summary: Lays children out vertically with consistent gaps between them.
description: Owns the space between children so components don't need outer margins. Replaces ad-hoc margin-top rules with a single gap token, which makes spacing predictable.

title: Inline
summary: Lays children out horizontally, wrapping onto new lines when needed.
description: The horizontal sibling of Stack: a flex row with gap and wrap, ideal for tags, buttons or metadata. Controls alignment and whether items wrap or scroll.

title: Grid
summary: Arranges content in rows and columns aligned to the layout grid.
description: Wraps CSS Grid with responsive column counts and gap tokens. Use it for 2D layouts like card galleries or dashboards; use Stack/Inline when only one axis matters.

title: Container
summary: Centres content and caps its width at a readable maximum.
description: Sets max-width and horizontal padding for page content so lines don't stretch across ultra-wide screens. Usually comes in a few sizes (sm, md, lg).

title: Spacer
summary: An empty element that inserts a fixed or flexible gap.
description: Useful to push items apart in a flex row (flex: 1) or add a one-off token-sized gap. Prefer gap on the parent; reach for Spacer when only one gap is different.

title: Divider
summary: A thin line that separates groups of content.
description: Horizontal or vertical. Use <hr> when it's a thematic break; otherwise mark it decorative (aria-hidden) so it isn't announced. Whitespace is often a quieter alternative.

title: AspectRatio
summary: Keeps a box at a fixed width-to-height ratio, like 16:9.
description: Reserves space for media before it loads, preventing layout shift. Now mostly a thin wrapper around the CSS aspect-ratio property.

title: Center
summary: Centres its child horizontally and vertically.
description: A tiny convenience primitive for icons in circles, empty states or loaders. Saves repeating the same flexbox incantation everywhere.

title: Card
summary: Groups related content and actions about one subject in a surface.
description: Header, media, body and actions in an elevated or outlined container. If the whole card is clickable, use one link with a stretched hit area instead of nesting interactive elements.

title: ScrollArea
summary: A region with its own scrolling and consistently styled scrollbars.
description: Keeps native scrolling but restyles scrollbars cross-platform. Scrollable regions need to be keyboard focusable (tabindex=0) so non-mouse users can scroll them.

title: Resizable panels
summary: Splits space into panes the user can resize by dragging a handle.
description: Common in IDEs and mail apps. The handle is a separator role with arrow-key support, and sizes are often persisted per user.

title: AppShell
summary: The persistent frame of an app: header, navigation and content area.
description: A template that places organisms (NavBar, SideNav) and leaves a slot for page content. Handles responsive collapse of the navigation and skip links to main.

title: Sidebar layout
summary: A two-column page: narrow sidebar plus flexible main column.
description: Sidebar holds filters, settings sections or a TOC. It stacks above or collapses into a drawer below a breakpoint. A classic page template in atomic design terms.

title: PageHeader
summary: The top of a page: title, breadcrumbs, description and primary actions.
description: Standardises where the page title (h1) and main actions live so every page feels consistent. Not to be confused with the site-wide NavBar.

title: Button
summary: Triggers an action like submit, save or open.
description: Variants express hierarchy (primary, secondary, ghost, destructive): one primary per view. Use a real <button>, keep it enabled with an explanation over silently disabling it, and show loading state inline.

title: IconButton
summary: A compact button that shows only an icon.
description: Perfect for toolbars and dense UIs, but the icon carries no name: it always needs an aria-label, ideally mirrored in a Tooltip. Hit area should stay at least 24–44px.

title: Chip
summary: A small interactive pill to filter, select or remove an item.
description: Unlike a static Tag, a Chip does something: toggles a filter (aria-pressed), removes a value, or suggests an input. Removable chips need an accessible remove button.

title: ToggleButton
summary: A button that stays pressed or unpressed, like Bold in an editor.
description: Communicates its state with aria-pressed. Use for immediate on/off formatting or view options; for settings that persist, a Switch reads more clearly.

title: ButtonGroup
summary: Visually joins related buttons into one control.
description: Groups actions like Undo/Redo or alignment options with shared borders and consistent spacing. If only one option can be active, you probably want a SegmentedControl.

title: SplitButton
summary: A main action button joined to a menu of related alternatives.
description: The left part runs the default (e.g. Merge), the arrow opens a Menu of variants (Squash, Rebase). Each part is a separate focusable button with its own label.

title: FAB
summary: A floating action button for the single most important action on screen.
description: Material Design pattern, mostly mobile: a round button pinned above content, e.g. Compose. Only one per screen, and it must not cover important content.

title: CopyButton
summary: Copies a value to the clipboard and confirms it worked.
description: Combines an IconButton with the Clipboard API and transient feedback (icon swap or Tooltip 'Copied!'). Announce the confirmation through a live region for screen readers.

title: Toolbar
summary: A container of controls that act on a view or selection.
description: Editor formatting bars, table bulk actions. Uses role=toolbar with roving tabindex: Tab enters once, arrow keys move between controls inside.

title: Field
summary: Wraps any control with its label, hint and error message.
description: The glue of form accessibility: generates ids and wires aria-describedby and aria-invalid so every control gets consistent label, help text and validation layout.

title: TextField
summary: A single-line text input, with label and messages built in.
description: Input is the bare atom; TextField = Field + Input, the molecule most teams actually use. Pick the right type and inputmode (email, tel, numeric) to get the right mobile keyboard.

title: Textarea
summary: A multi-line text input for longer free-form answers.
description: Often auto-grows with content and shows a character count. Size it to hint at the expected length of the answer.

title: Checkbox
summary: Selects zero, one or many options independently.
description: Also has an indeterminate state for 'some children selected'. In a form, checking it takes effect on submit; for instant on/off use a Switch.

title: Radio / RadioGroup
summary: Selects exactly one option from a small visible set.
description: A Radio alone is an atom; the group with its legend is the molecule. Arrow keys move selection within the group. Over ~5 options, consider a Select.

title: Switch
summary: Turns a setting on or off with immediate effect.
description: Like a light switch: no Save button needed. Uses role=switch with aria-checked. If the change needs confirming on submit, a Checkbox is the better fit.

title: Select
summary: Picks one option from a collapsed list.
description: Native <select> is the most accessible and mobile-friendly. Use custom ones only when you need rich option content; add search (Combobox) once the list gets long.

title: Combobox
summary: A text input that filters a popup list of suggestions as you type.
description: Input + Listbox in one. One of the hardest components to make accessible: aria-activedescendant tracks the highlighted option while focus stays in the input.

title: Listbox
summary: A list of selectable options, single or multi-select.
description: The option list that powers Select and Combobox, also usable inline. Supports keyboard navigation, type-ahead and aria-selected. Not for actions — that's a Menu.

title: Picker
summary: A trigger that opens a dedicated surface to choose a value.
description: Generic pattern behind date, time, colour and emoji pickers: a button showing the current value opens a Popover (or Sheet on mobile) with a specialised chooser.

title: SegmentedControl
summary: A row of joined buttons where exactly one is selected.
description: Good for 2–5 short options like Day / Week / Month that change a view. Behaves like a radio group. If it swaps whole panels of content, use Tabs instead.

title: Slider
summary: Chooses a value from a continuous range by dragging a thumb.
description: Great for approximate values like volume. For precise numbers, pair it with a NumberInput. Arrow keys step, Page Up/Down jump, and aria-valuetext can add units.

title: RangeSlider
summary: Selects a min–max range with two thumbs on one track.
description: Typical for price filters. Each thumb is a separate slider with its own label, and thumbs must not cross each other.

title: NumberInput
summary: Enters a number, with steppers to increment and decrement.
description: Handles min/max, step, locale formatting and arrow-key stepping. Don't use it for numbers that aren't quantities (phone, card, postcode) — those are text with inputmode=numeric.

title: PasswordInput
summary: A masked text field with a show/hide toggle.
description: The reveal toggle reduces typos. Set autocomplete to current-password or new-password so password managers work, and never block paste.

title: SearchField
summary: An input dedicated to search queries, with icon and clear button.
description: Uses type=search and sits inside a role=search landmark. Escape clears it. If it shows live suggestions, it becomes a Combobox.

title: PinInput
summary: A row of single-character boxes for codes like OTPs.
description: Auto-advances between boxes and must support pasting the full code. Use autocomplete=one-time-code so phones can fill SMS codes automatically.

title: TagInput
summary: Enters multiple values that turn into removable chips.
description: Type and press Enter or comma to add; Backspace removes the last chip. Used for emails, labels and keywords. Often combined with Combobox suggestions.

title: FileUpload
summary: Selects files via a button or by dropping them on a zone.
description: Drag-and-drop is an enhancement: always keep a real file input button. Show accepted types and size limits up front, then per-file progress and errors.

title: ColorPicker
summary: Chooses a colour via swatches, a 2D area, sliders or hex input.
description: Combines several molecules: saturation/brightness area, hue slider, alpha slider and text field. Always offer a typed input (hex) as an accessible fallback.

title: Calendar
summary: Displays a month grid to pick a date or browse days.
description: A grid with arrow-key navigation, month paging and disabled dates. Must respect locale: first day of week, month names and date format.

title: DatePicker
summary: A date input combined with a popup Calendar.
description: Field + Popover + Calendar. Let users type the date too — clicking back 40 years to a birthday is painful. For known dates like birthdays, plain fields often work better.

title: DateRangePicker
summary: Selects a start and end date, often over two calendars.
description: Common in bookings and analytics. Show the range highlighted while hovering, and offer presets like 'Last 7 days' which cover most needs.

title: TimePicker
summary: Enters a time of day, as segments or from a list of slots.
description: Segmented fields (hh : mm AM/PM) suit free entry; a list suits fixed slots like appointments. Respect the user's 12/24-hour locale.

title: Rating
summary: Captures or shows a score, usually as 1–5 stars.
description: As input it's essentially a radio group with star visuals. As display it's read-only with a text equivalent like '4.5 out of 5'.

title: Fieldset
summary: Groups related fields under a shared legend.
description: The <legend> gives context to every field inside, e.g. 'Shipping address' before Street and City. Required for radio and checkbox groups.

title: Form
summary: Collects fields, validation and submission into one unit.
description: Manages values, validation timing (on blur / on submit) and error summary. On failed submit, move focus to the first error or a summary that links to each field.

title: Stepper / Wizard
summary: Splits a long task into ordered steps with Back and Next.
description: Reduces cognitive load in checkouts and onboarding. Shows progress via a Steps indicator and keeps data when going back. Use it only when steps are truly sequential.

title: Tabs
summary: Switches between panels of related content in the same place.
description: A tablist of tabs, each controlling a tabpanel. Arrow keys move between tabs. Content is peer-level; if tabs change the URL as primary navigation, they're really a nav with links.

title: Accordion
summary: Stacks sections whose content expands and collapses on demand.
description: Each header is a button with aria-expanded. Great for FAQs and progressive disclosure on mobile; bad for content most users need, which then hides behind clicks.

title: Pagination
summary: Moves through content split into numbered pages.
description: Wrapped in a nav landmark, with aria-current on the active page. Better than infinite scroll when users need to find their way back or reach the footer.

title: Breadcrumbs
summary: Shows where the current page sits in the site hierarchy.
description: A trail of links like Home › Products › Shoes, in a nav labelled 'Breadcrumb'. The last item is the current page (aria-current=page) and isn't a link.

title: NavBar
summary: The site-wide top bar with logo, main links and account actions.
description: Logo + navigation + search + user menu: a classic organism. Collapses into a hamburger Menu or Sheet on mobile. Wrap it in <header> with a <nav> inside.

title: SideNav
summary: Vertical navigation down the side of an app.
description: Suits apps with many sections. Supports nested groups, icons and a collapsed rail mode. Mark the current link with aria-current=page.

title: NavLink
summary: A link inside navigation that knows when it's the current page.
description: A Link with an active state, set via aria-current=page so it's announced, not only coloured. The building block of NavBar, SideNav and Tabs-as-navigation.

title: Steps
summary: Shows progress through a sequence: done, current and upcoming steps.
description: The visual indicator used by a Stepper/Wizard. Marks the current step with aria-current=step and lets users jump back to completed ones.

title: TreeView
summary: Navigates nested hierarchies like folders by expanding nodes.
description: role=tree with arrow keys: Right expands, Left collapses or goes to parent. Heavy keyboard model — only use it when the data really is deeply hierarchical.

title: CommandPalette
summary: A ⌘K search box that jumps to any page or runs any command.
description: Dialog + Combobox + grouped results. A power-user accelerator, so everything in it must also be reachable through normal UI.

title: SkipLink
summary: A hidden-until-focused link to jump straight to main content.
description: The first Tab stop on the page, so keyboard users don't tab through the whole header each time. Visually hidden until focused, then clearly visible.

title: Table of contents
summary: Lists a page's sections and highlights the one in view.
description: Anchor links generated from headings, usually sticky beside long docs. Scroll-spy highlighting is an enhancement; the links must work without it.

title: Dialog
summary: A window over the page that demands attention before continuing.
description: Modal dialogs trap focus, close on Escape and return focus to the trigger. The native <dialog> with showModal() handles much of this. Keep them for focused tasks, not content.

title: DialogSystem
summary: A central service to open and stack dialogs from anywhere in the app.
description: Instead of each component rendering its own modal, a provider exposes an API like dialogs.open(...) and manages stacking, focus return and one-at-a-time rules.

title: AlertDialog
summary: A modal that asks the user to confirm an important action.
description: role=alertdialog, not dismissible by clicking outside. Buttons say what they do ('Delete project', not 'OK'), and initial focus goes to the safest choice.

title: Sheet
summary: A panel that slides in from a screen edge over the content.
description: Bottom sheets suit mobile actions; side sheets suit details and filters on desktop. Modal sheets behave like a Dialog; non-modal ones let you keep working.

title: Popover
summary: A floating, interactive panel anchored to a trigger.
description: Holds rich content like forms or pickers and opens on click. Unlike a Tooltip it can be focused and interacted with. The native popover attribute now handles top-layer and light dismiss.

title: Menu
summary: A popup list of actions or commands.
description: role=menu with menuitems navigated by arrow keys; selecting one runs an action. If the items are values to choose for a form, it's a Listbox/Select instead.

title: DropdownMenu
summary: A button that opens a Menu, like '⋯ More actions'.
description: Trigger + Menu. Supports sub-menus, groups, checkable items and shortcuts. Keep destructive items separated at the bottom.

title: ContextMenu
summary: A Menu opened by right-click or long-press at the pointer.
description: Speeds up power users in file managers and editors. It's hidden by nature, so every action must also be available somewhere visible. Shift+F10 opens it from the keyboard.

title: Tooltip
summary: A short text label that appears on hover or focus.
description: Plain text only, never interactive or essential. Shows on keyboard focus too, dismisses with Escape. Doesn't work on touch, so don't hide key info in it.

title: HoverCard
summary: A rich preview that appears when hovering a link, like a profile.
description: Sits between Tooltip (text only) and Popover (click to open). It's a progressive enhancement for sighted mouse users; the link must make sense without it.

title: Lightbox
summary: Shows an image or gallery full-screen over a dimmed page.
description: A specialised Dialog with next/previous, zoom and swipe. Close with Escape, keep alt text and captions, and return focus to the thumbnail.

title: Alert
summary: An inline message about status: info, success, warning or error.
description: Icon + title + text, coloured by severity (never colour alone). Persistent and in context. Only use role=alert for urgent messages added dynamically — it interrupts screen readers.

title: Banner
summary: A full-width message at the top of the app or page.
description: For system-level news: maintenance, trial ending, offline. Persists until resolved or dismissed. Don't stack several — prioritise one.

title: Badge
summary: A small count or status marker attached to another element.
description: Like '3' on an inbox icon or 'New' on a menu item. The info must reach screen readers too, e.g. 'Inbox, 3 unread' in the parent label.

title: Progress
summary: Shows how far along a task is, as a bar or ring.
description: Determinate when you know the percentage (uploads), indeterminate when you don't. Uses role=progressbar with aria-valuenow, and a label saying what is progressing.

title: Spinner
summary: An animated indicator that something is loading.
description: For short, unknown waits. Delay it ~300ms to avoid flicker, give it an accessible label, and prefer a Skeleton when you know the shape of the incoming content.

title: Skeleton
summary: Grey placeholder shapes that mimic content while it loads.
description: Feels faster than a spinner and prevents layout shift because the real content lands in the same shape. Hide it from screen readers and set aria-busy on the region.

title: Toast
summary: A brief notification that pops in and disappears by itself.
description: For low-priority confirmations like 'Message sent', often with Undo. Announced via a live region without stealing focus. Never put the only path to a critical action in one.

title: ToastProvider
summary: App-level service that queues, positions and announces toasts.
description: Mounted once near the root, exposing toast(...) to the whole app. Handles stacking, timeouts (paused on hover/focus) and the shared live region.

title: EmptyState
summary: What a view shows when there's no data yet, or no results.
description: Illustration + explanation + next action ('Create your first project'). Distinguish first use, no search results and errors — each needs different wording.

title: Callout
summary: A highlighted box that draws attention to a tip or note in content.
description: Editorial cousin of Alert, used inside docs and articles: Note, Tip, Warning. It's static content, so no live region needed.

title: StatusDot
summary: A small coloured dot that signals state, like online or failed.
description: Compact status for presence, builds or services. Colour alone fails colour-blind users, so pair it with text or a distinct shape.

title: Validation message
summary: Text below a field explaining what's wrong and how to fix it.
description: Say how to fix it ('Use at least 8 characters'), not just 'Invalid'. Linked to the field with aria-describedby, and shown with an icon, not just red text.

title: Table
summary: Displays data in rows and columns for scanning and comparing.
description: Use a real <table> with <th> headers and a caption. Right-align numbers, keep a sticky header for long tables, and let it scroll horizontally on small screens.

title: DataGrid
summary: An interactive table: sort, filter, select, edit, virtualise.
description: Table on steroids for large datasets. Uses role=grid where arrow keys move between cells. Only reach for it when users really manipulate data — a plain Table is far simpler.

title: Heatmap
summary: Encodes values as colour intensity across a grid.
description: Like a GitHub contribution graph. Needs a legend, a colour-blind-safe sequential palette and tooltips or a table alternative for exact values.

title: ListItem
summary: A row in a list with leading media, text lines and trailing actions.
description: Avatar or icon + primary/secondary text + meta or action. The workhorse of settings screens, inboxes and contacts.

title: DescriptionList
summary: Shows label–value pairs, like the details of an order.
description: Semantic <dl> with <dt>/<dd> pairs. Lays out as two columns on wide screens, stacked on narrow ones. Better than a table when there's only one record.

title: Stat
summary: Highlights one key number with its label and trend.
description: Label + big value + change ('▲ 12% vs last week'). Dashboards place several in a row. Make the trend direction readable in text, not just a green/red arrow.

title: Timeline
summary: Lists events in chronological order along a line.
description: Order history, activity feeds, changelogs. Semantically an ordered list with <time> elements. Mark the current or latest event clearly.

title: Tag
summary: A static label that categorises or describes an item.
description: Read-only metadata like 'Draft' or 'Design'. If clicking it filters or removes something, it's a Chip. Keep tag colours meaningful and consistent.

title: Avatar
summary: Represents a person or entity with an image or initials.
description: Falls back from photo to initials to a generic icon. Decorative next to a name (alt=""), meaningful when shown alone. Often carries a StatusDot.

title: AvatarGroup
summary: Overlapping avatars showing who's involved, with a +N overflow.
description: Shows collaborators or attendees compactly. The '+5' should reveal the full list (Popover or Tooltip) and the group needs a label like '8 members'.

title: Tree
summary: Displays hierarchical data with indentation and connectors.
description: Static display of nested data like an org chart or JSON viewer. When nodes are expandable and navigable it becomes a TreeView.

title: Chart
summary: Visualises data as bars, lines, areas or pies.
description: Pick the form by question: bars compare, lines show trends. Use a token-based palette, label axes, and provide a data table or summary for screen readers.

title: Carousel
summary: Shows one slide of a set at a time, with controls to move between.
description: Most users never see past slide one, so don't hide key content in it. Never auto-advance without a pause button; support swipe and keyboard.

title: Image
summary: Displays a picture responsively, with loading and fallback states.
description: Wraps with srcset, lazy loading, aspect ratio and a fallback. Every image needs alt: describe informative images, use alt="" for decorative ones.

title: Figure
summary: An image, chart or snippet with an associated caption.
description: Semantic <figure> + <figcaption>. The caption complements, not replaces, the alt text — and is visible to everyone.

title: VideoPlayer
summary: Plays video with controls for play, seek, volume and captions.
description: Captions and transcripts are required for accessibility. Never autoplay with sound; all controls must work by keyboard.

title: Icon
summary: A small symbol from the system's icon set.
description: Sized and coloured by tokens, inheriting currentColor. Decorative by default (aria-hidden); if it conveys meaning alone, it needs a label.

title: Logo
summary: Renders the brand mark in its approved variants.
description: Encodes brand rules (clear space, min size, light/dark versions) in one place. Usually links home, with alt text naming the company, not 'logo'.

title: VisuallyHidden
summary: Hides content visually but keeps it for screen readers.
description: Adds context sighted users get from layout, like 'Delete invoice #42' behind a trash icon. Different from display:none, which hides from everyone.

title: Portal
summary: Renders children into another DOM node, usually the body.
description: Escapes parent overflow and z-index for overlays like Dialog, Popover and Toast. The native popover/dialog top layer is making it less necessary.

title: FocusTrap
summary: Keeps keyboard focus cycling inside a region while it's open.
description: Used by modal Dialogs and Sheets so Tab can't wander to the page behind. Paired with returning focus to the trigger when closed.

title: ThemeProvider
summary: Supplies design tokens and theme (light, dark, brand) to the tree.
description: Sits at the root and sets CSS variables or context so every component reads the right tokens. Respects prefers-color-scheme and avoids a flash of the wrong theme.

title: Show / Hide
summary: Conditionally renders children by breakpoint or condition.
description: Declarative responsive helpers like <Show above="md">. Prefer CSS-only hiding when possible to avoid layout shift on hydration.

title: Transition
summary: Animates elements as they enter, leave or change.
description: Wraps motion tokens (duration, easing) for consistent animation. Must respect prefers-reduced-motion by shortening or removing movement.
